question: why is the in-loop verify 56 ms when verify_decomposition says t(k=4)=44.09 ms?
answer: verify_decomposition times the FORWARD ONLY (mx.eval(hh) at line 380) but compares it against a bandwidth floor that includes the LM head. The loop also pays the LM head.
loop_ingredients_verdict: NEGLIGIBLE - measured twice (+0.80 and +0.02 ms). The gap is not loop-specific.
headroom_location: ALL of it is the transformer forward: 17.05 ms/cycle. The LM head is at roofline.
verify_decomposition_ratio_column_is_wro: it divides forward-only time by the TOTAL floor (dense+lm_head). At k=4 it reports 1.110; the correct forward-vs-forward-floor ratio is 44.09/31.71 = 1.39.
why_phase0_predicted_58.8: the k=4 optimum and the 17.0 ms/token prediction were built on the understated forward-only t(k). With the LM head and host python included the corrected model predicts ~43 tok/s and the loop measures 42.46 - agreement within ~3%, so there was never a 32% host overhead to reclaim.
note: cycle 58.4 ms / emitted 2.587 = 42.5 tok/s (measured 42.46). To hit 48.0 tok/s the cycle must emit 2.80 tokens, i.e. mean accepted 1.80 of gamma=3 (hard max 3.0).

calibration: signal is real: P(accept) 0.333 in [0.00,0.50) -> 0.974 in [0.99,1.00), spread 0.641, break-even q*=0.422
why_acceptance_gain_does_not_convert: two costs absorb it. (1) single-barrier truncation must run ALL gamma_max drafter steps (5 x 1.338 = 6.98 ms vs ~4.3 ms at fixed gamma=3). (2) the truncation decision needs the confidences on the HOST, which reinstates the barrier P0.3 removed, so draft no longer fuses into verify. mean drafted rises to ~3.0 so k~4.0 -- the SAME verify cost as fixed gamma=3 -- while draft cost and one barrier are added.

Against the k=4 optimum the schedule has almost no room, exactly as the cost curve implies: at the optimum, shortening the block moves you below it.

question: Does this harness produce a better result than the runtimes people already use (ollama, LM Studio, mlx-vlm), or the same number with more ceremony?

prediction.1_plain_decode_converges: At batch 1 every runtime is memory-bandwidth-bound. Stock MLX decode measures 97% of the calibrated 89 GB/s ceiling. Therefore plain decode across all runtimes lands within a few percent of each other ONCE NORMALISED by measured active bytes/token.
prediction.2_speedup_source: Our 1.74x comes ENTIRELY from speculative decoding, not from kernel quality. Plain-decode kernel quality is expected to be indistinguishable across runtimes.
prediction.3_falsifier: Any runtime beating us on NORMALISED bytes-per-token (i.e. a materially higher %-of-89 GB/s at batch-1 plain decode) falsifies clause 1 and is a real finding.

reporting_rule: Raw tok/s alone is not a comparison. Every runtime must be reported as: raw tok/s, measured active bytes/token (derived from the actual on-disk quant, never estimated), effective GB/s, and % of the 89 GB/s ceiling. A quant we cannot account for byte-for-byte is reported 'not comparable', not estimated.

verdict: Plain decode is the SAME NUMBER across runtimes, exactly as pre-registered. On byte-identical weights (3,535,067,220 active bytes/token derived independently inside each venv by the same roofline.param_breakdown) mlx-vlm 0.6.17 decodes at 23.54 tok/s and our stock mlx-lm arm at 23.56 (block 1) / 24.17 (block 3 drift control) -- 0.1% to 1.4% apart, inside the session's own 2.6-3.1% drift band, both at 93.5-96.0% of the 89 GB/s ceiling. We have NO kernel-quality advantage and never did. But the harness is NOT 'the same number with more ceremony': the SPECULATIVE loops differ sharply on those same weights with the same drafter architecture (gemma4_assistant -> draft_kind 'mtp'). Ours 42.94/41.62 tok/s vs mlx-vlm 34.39 at its own default block and 33.30 at our matched gamma -- ours is +22.9% over mlx-vlm's default. Per-runtime speedup over each runtime's OWN plain baseline: ours 1.72-1.82x, mlx-vlm 1.41-1.46x. So the value is precisely where clause 2 said it would be (the speculative loop) and precisely not where it said it would not be (the kernels).

stability.pooled_cv_caveat: The harness's pooled-cv gate flagged 5.5% (ours spec, block 1) as 'not publishable'. That is an artefact of the gate, not instability: it pools two prompts whose speculative rates genuinely differ (p0 ~40.6, p1 ~44.6 tok/s), so the pooled cv measures the PROMPT DIFFERENCE, not steadiness. Per-prompt cv is <=2.1% everywhere. Statistic did not match the question - a gate bug to fix, and it changes no median.

limitations: Only 2 of the 4 intended runtimes were measurable. ollama absent; LM Studio cannot load the checkpoint. The comparison therefore covers MLX runtimes only and says nothing about llama.cpp/GGUF kernel quality.
mlx-vlm's acceptance is not exposed, so its speculative deficit cannot be attributed between lower acceptance and higher per-cycle cost. That is the obvious next measurement.

mlx-vlm's mtp path is general-purpose across many drafter families; ours is specialised to this target/drafter pair. The +22.9% is a measured fact about the two implementations as shipped, NOT a claim that mlx-vlm is poorly written.

Our speculative arm is timed wall-clock INCLUDING prefill (spec_decode returns its tokens in one batch rather than streaming), while every other arm excludes prefill. On a 26-token prompt this UNDERSTATES our speculative arm by roughly 1%, so the gap is if anything slightly larger than reported. Conservative direction, stated rather than corrected.

ground_2_our_build_already_has_the_fix.claim_checked: CLAUDE.md frames our 69%-vs-97% verify-batching gap as 'same dispatch-heuristic family as MLX #3553'.
ground_2_our_build_already_has_the_fix.evidence: Our PINNED mlx 0.32.2 already contains the qmv_wide kernel family that superseded the qmv_fast path #3553 was about. Direct binary evidence: site-packages/mlx/lib/mlx.metallib contains 2016 'qmv_wide' strings (and 912 'qmv_fast'); site-packages/mlx/lib/libmlx.dylib carries the qmv_wide dispatch symbol. Corroborated by issue comment 3 (katlun-lgtm, 2026-07-09) already analysing qmv_wide on '0.32.0.dev'.
ground_2_our_build_already_has_the_fix.consequence: Every measurement in runs.jsonl was taken on the POST-qmv_wide kernel set. Whatever our verify-batching gap is, it is NOT the M=3 qmv_fast step that #3553 described - that code path was superseded and our build has the successor. The '#3553 family' framing is a MECHANISM CLAIM that the facts contradict, and CLAUDE.md's own rule is that mechanism claims are not measurements.

not_asserted: Whether our specific verify shapes actually DISPATCH to qmv_wide is UNVERIFIED. Presence of the kernel family in the binary is not proof of dispatch for our shapes. Asserting that would be a second unmeasured mechanism claim.
what_would_settle_it: Sweep t(k) at k=1..6 on our actual verify shapes and look for a step at M=3, and confirm which kernel the dispatch chooses. CLAUDE.md's stored t(k) skips k=2 and k=3, so the existing data cannot answer it.
